sites.title: Web addresses
sites.description: One or more pages to follow, separated by commas. Links are followed inside the folder of each address, so end an address with / to stay inside that folder (https://example.com/docs/).

followLinks.title: How many links deep to follow
followLinks.description: 0 saves only the addresses above; 2 also saves the pages they link to, and the pages those link to.

refreshEveryHours.title: Check for changes every (hours)
refreshEveryHours.description: 0 refreshes only when you press Sync now.

exclude.title: Skip addresses containing
exclude.description: Patterns separated by commas. Start one with / to skip a folder (/blog/); anything else skips addresses that contain it (?page=). * matches anything.

useBrowser.title: Open pages in a browser (off: save the text only)
useBrowser.description: A browser sees pages that are built by scripts and takes screenshots. Text only is faster and works where a browser cannot run.

setupInstructions.title: No sign-in needed
setupInstructions.description: Paste the pages you want Gezel to know. It visits them in its own browser, never clicks or types anything, and saves what a visitor would read.
steps: Paste one or more addresses, separated by commas. A bare site name like example.com works.
Choose how far to follow links and how many pages to keep. Start small; you can raise it later.
Gezel checks each site politely, at most one page every second or two, and follows the site's crawler rules.

notes: One folder per site, one file per page, laid out by the page's address (the first two folders of the address become folders). Each record holds the page's main text as markdown (navigation, footers and anything a visitor cannot see are left out), its title, description and dates as frontmatter, and up to six screenshots plus up to six images from the main text as attachments. Each site also gets a site-overview file listing every saved page, and a monthly change log under site-changes/ listing pages added, changed (with the lines that appeared and disappeared) and removed. A page is rewritten only when its text changes. Pages are rendered in a sandboxed browser whose every request passes through Gezel's own filter, which refuses private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses; a site you type that sits on a private network (an intranet wiki) is reachable while its own pages are captured. The browser never clicks, types, submits forms, downloads files or grants permissions; consent banners are hidden, not accepted. Where no sandboxed browser can run, pages are saved as text only, without screenshots. A page that answers with a bot check, a sign-in form or almost no text keeps its earlier copy. A page that answers 'not found' twice is removed. Links to sign-out, cart and edit pages, links carrying a token, and files (PDFs, images, downloads) are never followed. Limits: 45 seconds, 30 MB and 400 requests per page; a refresh saves at most 40 pages and runs for at most four minutes, continuing on the next one. Because the crawl is capped and only follows links, this is a window, not a mirror.
